text:
Vincent Trocheck is 33, on his fourth NHL team, and suddenly playing a lot more. His ice time is up more than four minutes a night over his last ten games, to about 21, and he's answered with goals in three straight, including a power-play goal and a two-point night as Utah beat Colorado to end a six-game skid, per NHL.com.

The season line is modest: 6 goals and 14 points in 24 games. The process behind it is anything but. At 5v5 the Mammoth get 59% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and 4 points more than when he sits. He has 6 goals on 7.4 expected, so if anything the finish has lagged the chances.

That's a change from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had his results running ahead of his chances and opponents generating more with him out there, against the toughest competition in the league (99th percentile). He still plays the same way: 61 hits, and 53% of his shots off the rush in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking. Watch whether the extra minutes stick once Utah's skid is a memory.
headline: Trocheck finds his feet in Utah
